This guide explains the working V4 simulator. Blocks are software jobs, not existing ROS nodes. Camera images and masks come from a synthetic V4 scene. Path examples use V4 geometry or planner output. Source notes distinguish illustrations from recorded runs.

01 / SETUP

Set the map, start and goals

We load one shared course and one measured car.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Car: 30 × 19.2 cm. Wheelbase: 21.6 cm. Lane: 30 cm. Rear-axle turning radius: editable; 40 cm default. The start and map are preloaded in V4. A real manual map/UWB calibration lap is still to implement.

02 / SENSE

Give each sensor a job

Three cameras see the road. Other sensors support them.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

V4 renders three 192 × 144 camera feeds at 8 Hz. UWB samples at 5 Hz. LiDAR scans about every 0.18 s. Camera mounts are provisional. These rates are simulator settings, not RDK X5 measurements.

03 / SENSE

Turn three views into road

We warp each camera into the same top-down space.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Projection uses provisional pinhole calibration and a flat local-ground assumption. The stitch chooses one camera per cell; it does not average all three. Dark neutral pixels become road; bright pixels become paint. Growth uses four touching neighbours. These camera and mask images were generated by V4.

04 / SENSE

Remember what just disappeared

We keep recent road edges in a fixed local frame.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Driving uses observations up to 2–3 seconds old, with a motion-based uncertainty limit. The display can show 25 seconds. Bay-edge lookup can use 24 seconds during parking. LiDAR scans are separate; they are not accumulated into this grid.

05 / LOCATE

Keep a smooth local position

We use wheels, IMU and seen edges for precise driving.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Position here means location plus heading. Camera matching corrects translation; simulated IMU heading supplies orientation. Straight edges mainly constrain sideways error. Matching pauses on steep pitch and during parking. V4 is prior-map-aided; it is not full visual SLAM.

06 / LOCATE

Let UWB help in the background

We keep noisy UWB away from the steering position.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

The violet estimate includes UWB. The yellow local estimate never receives a UWB position jump. Distinctive visual geometry also helps the coarse estimate. The confidence values are approximate model indicators. The orange cloud here is a synthetic illustration at 20 cm σ per axis.

07 / PLAN

Global planner: choose the road route

We connect clockwise checkpoints to each destination.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

V4 precomputes two directed routes from configured checkpoints. It checks the whole nominal body and turning radius. It does not compare every possible route or choose exits from UWB alone. Global road approach ends at the parking handoff; local parking starts there.

core.js · buildMission, hybridPlan

08 / PLAN

Mission logic: choose what happens now

We choose the active route, behaviour and motion source.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

The state machine chooses ROAD, PARKING or RECOVERY. Seen red lights and closed gates cause holds. Recognition is ideal only when visible and not occluded. Ramp/bump speed zones use the prior map; V4 does not implement a separate sign detector for every challenge.

09 / PLAN

Find the lane we should follow

We combine the chosen branch with the road we see.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

The guide keeps the route’s useful offset through tight turns. The car need not sit on the exact geometric centreline. The route selects the exit; local road evidence checks the opening. A course-location conflict holds. Missing local visibility may trigger checked recovery.

10 / PLAN

Local planner: choose the next movement

We pick the lowest-cost candidate that passes the checks.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Runs at 5 Hz. Nine lateral alternatives follow the chosen branch; they do not enumerate every roundabout exit. If all strict paths fail, V4 tries nine more with the adjustable 0–5 cm paint allowance. Boundary crossings still count. Persistent failure can start recovery. These candidate drawings come from a V4 run.

11 / MANOEUVRE

Parking planner: compute the manoeuvre

We plan into the observed bay. We do not replay motion.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Reeds–Shepp curves use forward and reverse arcs. V4 tries a 15/12/8 cm docking straight, then other connections and a bounded hybrid fallback. Up to 48 family transforms are evaluated per start/goal pair; fewer valid curves may result. This is a computed geometry example, not a recorded parking result.

12 / MANOEUVRE

Recovery planner: make room, then rejoin

We plan the way back before reversing.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

The search tries up to five future route poses. A recovery starts in reverse, then changes once to forward. Default planned reverse limit: 20 cm. Speed: 3 cm/s. It rescans if no route fits. Obstacles, stale sensors and emergency stops still prevent motion. The sequence is a computed example using V4’s search with synthetic rear-road evidence. Reverse recovery and paint tolerance are training overrides, not new competition permissions.

13 / ACT

Turn the path into a request

We aim at a nearby path point, then ask for motion.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

The tracker uses a nearby look-ahead point. Limits come from the wheelbase and turning radius. It handles forward/reverse direction and stopped gear changes. V4 simulates actuator response; the real response still needs measurement.

14 / ACT

Safety: decide whether motion is allowed

A valid path never overrides a safety stop.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

Camera age above 0.45 s stops motion. Local uncertainty, physical contact, tunnel clearance and unresolved route identity also cause holds. Recovery can solve a planning deadlock; it cannot bypass these limits. Thresholds are simulator settings.

app.js · safety checks / recovery.js · obstacle checks
FEEDS INTO15 One Command Owner ↗

15 / ACT

Command owner: one final writer

Every block asks. Only one owner commands the car.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

V4’s mission code selects the active source. The owner then checks safety and the 200 ms request age. It does not implement a queue of competing ROS publishers. ROAD, PARKING, RECOVERY, WATCHDOG and SAFETY STOP are visible on the dashboard.

vehicle.js · arbitrate / app.js · step
FEEDS INTO16 Vehicle + New Observations ↗

16 / ACT

Move, observe, repeat

Each command changes the next sensor readings.

What the V4 code actually does ＋

The physics state renders sensors and checks errors. Green truth is for assessment, not position input to the planner. Motion uses simplified steering and speed response. The nominal body collider does not certify mast clearance, tyre grip or suspension. The measured overheight mast still needs a physical fix.

This guide preserves V4’s limits. Map/UWB calibration and real actuator measurements remain hardware work.
